analysis:
The supplied units cover docs/architecture/inference.md only. Units :4 and :5 are base text (lines 829-1195) and :6 is head text (lines 1-398). No patch hunks were supplied, so I could not compare base against head. I flagged nothing, because I saw no behavioral change and no security-relevant diff.

The head excerpt is a documentation page. The one visible change is the header date "Last updated: 2026-10-18" (head line 3). The rest of the head text describes existing behavior: GLM5Next admission and ownership, prompt measurements, startup calibration, and the bridge boundary. This is documentation drift at most.

Areas where the docs touch the threat model:
- T-041 (prefix cache): the page references the SSD prefix cache and MiMo SSD reuse defaults. The visible text does not alter the TTL, the HMAC naming, the per-donation gate or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch. Base lines 901 and 1014-1018 describe MiMo exact identities defaulting to SSD reuse and the encrypted store. If the full diff changes these claims, the next pass should check them against T-041's 30-minute TTL and its account-scoped salt.
- Base lines 1074-1083 say the integration starts no local HTTP endpoint and does not change consumer or OpenRouter routing.
- Base lines 1020-1024 say no catalog entry or release is activated.

Coverage limit: head text stops at line 398 and base text starts at 829. The ranges do not overlap, so I could not verify most of the head file's later portion or any line-level changes. A later pass should run the full diff against the cache-related sections (the MiMo prefix and paged-prefix paragraphs, base lines ~901-902 and 1014-1018) and against any head changes to the TTL, disk budget or kill-switch statements.
